meaningMnemonic: The building clown is the only clown allowed to accompany you. You hate all clowns, and so does the rest of your town. But this clown is really good at building buildings, and he's allowed to leave his part of town and accompany you while you fix buildings together. Hints I know it's been a long time, but try not to mix this one up with 部 , if you can. Remember, the clown building is in another part of town and the clowns aren't supposed to leave. But the building clown is okay to accompany you through the rest of the city.
readingMnemonic: He can only accompany you for so long though and soon it's time to say bye ( ばい ) again. Hints Wave bye to the clown, he'll accompany you on your building job tomorrow, but right now he has to go home and be with the rest of his clown people. He can't accompany you after dark.

meaningMnemonic: Put your fingers on your husband to aid him. There's something about a spouse's touch that just makes you feel better. Have you ever had someone rub your back while you were hurt or sick or sad? It's nice, right? Hints Imagine rubbing your husband's back with your fingers to aid him. You want him to feel better. You want him to get that comforting feeling that this kind of touching gives.
readingMnemonic: Unfortunately, your husband wouldn't need your aid if he wasn't such a foo l ( ふ ). He walks into doors, he falls down the stairs, he touches the plate when the waiter says it's hot. And every single time your fool husband hurts himself, you aid him. Hints That's true love, my friend.

meaningMnemonic: When your scooter has a fault , you need to get an alternate . Hopefully your insurance will cover it too. Hints You have a scooter that you drive every single day, but if you notice a fault, you need to send it in to get it fixed. That's when you break out your alternate scooter.
readingMnemonic: The alternate scooter is made entirely of 鉄 ( てつ ). It's hard and cold and not very comfortable when you sit on it. That's why you chose to keep it as an alternate and not as your everyday scooter. Hints Imagine riding on your alternate 鉄 scooter. Feel the hard iron under your bum and the loud sounds it makes as you scoot down the street. I hope your normal scooter is fixed soon.

meaningMnemonic: Your husband was wearing his cleat s when he accidentally stepped on a bird . Luckily this particular bird is a chicken , and chickens are really durable! Hints Picture the sad, stepped on chicken. It's angrily clucking and chasing your husband around your yard for what he did.
readingMnemonic: The only way to stop the chicken from putting on your husband's cleats and stepping on him to death in revenge is to feed it the ca ke ( けい ) you were making. Hints This cake was for your husband, but now he gets nothing. The chicken gets to eat all of the cake in front of him instead.

meaningMnemonic: The king rake d all the mountain s down into flat land so he could see everyone in the kingdom from his castle windows. You should share your congratulations with him. Now, quick tell him this was a great idea. Hints Imagine saying "Congratulations!" to a king who just ordered his servants to rake down all the pretty mountains in his kingdom.
readingMnemonic: The moment you say " Congratulations !" you've already started to miss ( みず ) those beautiful mountains. But you can't let missing them ruin your congratulations! Don't let the king know! Hints Imagine how hollow your congratulation sounds when you really miss those mountains. This king doesn't deserve your nice words.

meaningMnemonic: Gambler s usually only see the sun at dawn . They gamble all day and through the night, and if they leave it's at the crack of dawn to get home, clean up, and then go back. Hints Imagine being a gambler and seeing the bright dawn sun when you come out of the casino or pachinko parlor. It burns your eyes. Evil dawn... Get back inside, quick!
readingMnemonic: If you're up at dawn you'll also see the あか (red) つき (moon). The あかつき only happens as the sun comes up at dawn, so usually only gamblers see it. But if you get up early, you can see it too! Hints Imagine getting up at dawn and seeing the あかつき in the sky near the sun. It's so beautiful!

meaningMnemonic: A clown takes a knife and divide s himself. First he divides himself into two pieces, then he's in four pieces, then... oh why won't he stop?! Hints Instead of dying, the clown divides into slightly thinner clowns.
readingMnemonic: The clown finally stops trying to divide himself, and you can't stand to look at all of him. You grab a bow ling ( ぼう ) ball and bowl all of his divided parts over! Hints The many clowns crash to the floor as the bowling ball plows through their... his(?) divided bodies. You can't bear to look anymore.

meaningMnemonic: If you touch ice for too long you'll get frostbite and that's a really hard thing to endure . A lot of people can't, and die. Then again, you managed to endure touching ice long enough to get frostbite in the first place, so maybe this is baby stuff for you. Hints Imagine having to endure the pain of frostbite because you were a jerk who put his hand on ice for a few hours.
readingMnemonic: The best people in the world at being able to endure the pain are the shino bi ( しの ) ninjas! They train by hanging out in frozen areas all the time and don't complain at all. Maybe if the pain gets to be too much you can go ask them for advice. Hints Imagine if you were one of these cool Shinobi ninjas that could endure the extreme cold and pain of frostbite!

meaningMnemonic: You have to reach a certain number of flowers and tsunami s hits to become a legitimate fiefdom . At least in the old days. If you don't meet one of these conditions, like if you get hit by tsunamis all the time but you only have two or three flowers that will grow, you can't be your own fiefdom. Hints Imagine being the person who has to check whether each fiefdom has enough flowers and tsunamis per year to keep their status.
readingMnemonic: The most famous fiefdom checker is Han ( はん ) Solo. He takes his Millennium Falcon and swoops around checking for flowers and signs of past tsunamis and then he'll either say you can or cannot be your own fiefdom. Thanks Han Solo! Hints Picture Han Solo flying around Japan checking to make sure all the fiefdoms are up to code.

meaningMnemonic: If you say the lineup of your family members that have lived on this earth under the sun , you're really explaining your genealogy . This kanji has a second meaning too. It means score, as in a musical score or sheet music. So if your sheet music say s the line up of chords, especially sun nny notes, that's the score of a song. Those sunny notes are loved by your ancestors. Hints Say the line up of your family under the sun, then sing some sunny chords to match. You'll know your genealogy and a musical score!
readingMnemonic: If you can't tell the difference between your genealogy and a musical score , you're a foo l ( ふ ) and I can't help you. You aren't a fool, are you? You know the difference. Hints Your family genealogy and a musical score aren't even close to being the same thing. Memorize these or everyone will think you're a fool.

meaningMnemonic: The king wants you to make a rocket that looks glassy . It won't be very stable, and it probably won't work, but making it glassy and pretty is the only way to make the king approve. Hints Imagine a king who won't accept a rocket that isn't made of glassy material. He's not very smart...
readingMnemonic: You take the glassy rocket and try to stuff some thin reed s ( り ) inside to support it. But because it's clear and glassy the king sees them at the last second. Hints Picture the king admiring himself in the glassy surface and then his face contorts. He smashes his fist through the rocket and rips out the reeds. "REEDS AREN'T GLASSY!" he cries, and starts hitting you with them.

meaningMnemonic: You can only manage to avoid a tsunami by standing above it on a small stool if you are very graceful . If you aren't graceful enough the tsunami will knock you and the stool over and you'll be swept away like everyone else. Hints Imagine being graceful enough to balance on a small stool above a raging tsunami! Sooo cool!
readingMnemonic: No matter how graceful you are, the tsunami still shook ( しゅく ) the small stool. That's where your gracefulness came in. The stool shook, but you didn't. You balanced yourself and refused to go down. Hints It doesn't matter how badly the stool shook, you stayed graceful and didn't fall!

meaningMnemonic: The leader does a dance on top of the tree to show his greatness to everyone around. If he dances all the way up there on top of the tree, then no one can deny his excellence ! Hints "Look upon your leader's greatness!" he shouts, doing a jig around on the branches.
readingMnemonic: If you don't recognize the leader's greatness he will throw ketsu p ( けつ ) all over you (it's a special mix of ketchup and catsup). And it's ketsup because it looks like blood. The blood he'll spill if you don't look up and clap at his great dancing. Hints "Oh leader, your greatness is so... great!" you shout up at him. He's holding the ketsup bottle over your head and staring into your eyes as he dances in the tree. He isn't sure if he wants to dump it on you yet. He isn't sure if you really recognize his excellence.

meaningMnemonic: A samurai puts his forehead on the table next to his weapon . He is just a husk of his former self. This shell of a samurai has nothing left. Hints He's just sitting there, he can't even pick up his weapon or raise his head anymore.
readingMnemonic: The only way to bring a husk of a samurai back to life is to have a cock ( かく ) crow right in his ear. Hints "Co co co co cooooock!" the cock screams, shocking the samurai back into his lifeless shell. You did it!

meaningMnemonic: The king will send his men with sword s into your private rice paddy if you come across lapis lazuli . Even though this is your private land, he wants that lapis lazuli to make some new crowns and thrones for himself. Plus he's the king, so he can do whatever he wants. If you've never taken an art history class (or played Minecraft) you may never have come across lapis lazuli, but think of it as a pretty, blue precious stone that people really, really liked in the olden days. Hints Watch the king's swords digging in your private rice paddy and digging up huge chunks of lapis lazuli. This isn't fair, that lapis should belong to you.
readingMnemonic: You run up and ask how this lapis lazuli thievery isn't illegal and one of the swordsmen just shouts, " Loo phole ( る )!" What? What loophole? What law says that the king gets to steal your stuff? Hints Imagine reading through a giant text called "The Law" and looking for this loophole the king's men claim to have about taking your lapis lazuli. You can't find it... but maybe if you search just a bit longer...

meaningMnemonic: Wait, you have a gold roof over your coat rack ? Better put a lock on it, then. Hints When people see your gold-roofed coat rack, they're probably going to want to steal it, so you should put a lock on it to keep it safe.
readingMnemonic: The best guy to go to for a good lock is Joe ( じょう ) the farmhand. Joe isn't just good at farming — he's skilled in all manner of hands-on work, including locksmithing. Hints Joe will hook you up with a sturdy and reliable lock for your gold-roofed coat rack, guaranteed.

meaningMnemonic: A sweet woman sits under a tree and works as a mediator . If you're having a fight with someone, bring them to the sweet woman under the tree and she'll mediate for the two of you. Problem solved! Thanks sweet lady! Hints Imagine the sweet tree woman being a mediator for you and your arch rival. What she says fixes everything between you two!
readingMnemonic: You go to pay the woman for being your mediator for you two but she just says, " Bye ばい )." You try to hand her some money and she stares into your eyes. "Bye." Oh... okay, bye then. Hints Imagine her refusing to let you pay her for her mediator services and just saying "bye" over and over until you leave. Weird.

meaningMnemonic: If a tsunami gets into a net that's im prison ing a bunch of insect s, the insects are going to get all muddy . The net gets dragged along with the tsunami water and the insects can't escape, so they just get covered in the yucky stuff. Hints Picture a net prison full of insects being dragged by a tsunami getting muddier and muddier. Poor buggles!
readingMnemonic: Unfortunately for the insects, these muddy conditions have created the perfect habitat for duck s ( だく ). And muddy insects already imprisoned in a muddy net is a duck's favorite treat! Hints Picture a bunch of muddy ducks munching on some muddy trapped insects, in some muddy leftover tsunami water.

meaningMnemonic: If you spill something red on yourself in winter you should pardon yourself immediately and try to find something else to wear. It's very dangerous to wear red in winter, and even if it seems rude, make sure you pardon yourself right away and get that taken care of! Hints Imagine spilling red wine or red paint down your shirt. Quickly pardon yourself and get changed now!
readingMnemonic: If you don't pardon yourself fast enough the winter sha man ( しゃ ) will burst in and cast a spell on you, taking away all the clothes that have red on them! Now you have to pardon yourself for being naked! Hints Imagine not pardoning yourself fast enough and having the winter shaman spirit away whatever you got red on. That's embarrassing.

meaningMnemonic: Throw a drunkard in a cage with a tiger and some spikes and the tiger will have the time of its life play ing with them! Think of all the tiger play time possibilities! Hints If you were the tiger how would you play with the drunkard?
readingMnemonic: If you aren't the tiger, watching it play is a little like watching someone's head get cut off with a gui llotine ( ぎ ). In fact, you don't want to watch it play at all anymore. Hints What would you rather watch? A guillotine at work or a tiger playing like this?

meaningMnemonic: The receive radical and receive kanji are exactly the same. Hints Receive this nice, easy kanji with thanks!
readingMnemonic: The best place to receive anything is in きょう と . The city is famous for the quality of everything they make, so if you’re in きょうと , keep your fingers crossed that you’ll receive something. Hints Imagine being in きょうと and receiving something wonderful from a passerby in the street. What did you receive? How does it feel to receive something so great?

meaningMnemonic: If you want to take a flag out of the mouth of a mantis you have to make a formal request first. Mantises don't like to just give things away, and they're kind of mean so if you try to steal the flag it will probably bite you. So make a formal, polite request if you want it. Hints Imagine trying to request a flag from a scary mantis that has it sitting in it's mouth. Will it give it to you? Will it bite you? You'll have to wait and see.
readingMnemonic: After you request the mantis give you its flag it shock s ( しょく ) you by actually spitting it out of its mouth at your feet. You didn't think your request would work, or even if the mantis understood human speech, but it shocked you by doing exactly what you asked! Hints Imagine your shock at finding out the mantis not only understood your request, but agreed! This is great but also makes you wonder what other creatures can understand you...

meaningMnemonic: You see a triceratops standing in front of a full moon and you can't help but see a really strong resemblance . The triceratops has that round frill thing behind its horns and it looks just like the round full moon. Who knew that a triceratops would resemble the moon! Hints Look at the triceratops. Now look at the moon. See the resemblance? Uncanny, don't you think?
readingMnemonic: The first person to see this resemblance was the Shou gun ( しょう ). That's why he decided to put a triceratops head with the moon behind it on his mon (family crest). Now he's known as the full moon dinosaur shogun, and he's very famous. Hints Imagine being the Shougun and seeing the resemblance between a triceratops and the moon for the first time. You'd put that on all your stuff too, if you were him.

meaningMnemonic: You see a soul on a cross covered in flowers with shellfish at its feet and you suddenly resent them. It's not like you want to be the one up there on the cross, but so many people left flowers and shellfish for them. It should have been you... Hints Picture the soul on the cross, flowers all around it and shellfish at its feet. Feel your resentment grow.
readingMnemonic: You realize you resent them because it looks like they're having fun ( ふん ). You aren't having fun, and you wanna be! How dare they have fun when you aren't! Hints You wanna have fun hanging out on a cross with flowers and all the shellfish you can eat. Your resentment grows and grows as you watch the soul having everything you suddenly want. Fun fact: when you see 賁 in a kanji, the reading is probably going to be ふん .

meaningMnemonic: A tree is stuck in a prison under the ground and it's starting to rot and decay . Hints Trees can't live without sunlight, and it's too damp underground in a prison. The water gets all moldy and the tree will rot and die.
readingMnemonic: You get close to the rot ting tree and see some rotten cu cumbers ( きゅう ) hanging from its branches. No! Hints This poor cucumber tree, left in this ground prison to rot. There's nothing worse than eating a rotten cucumber.

meaningMnemonic: You're walking down the street when you see twenty big cross es lined up in front of you. Crosses creep you out and this is way too many for you to keep walking so you decide to run as fast as you can to get past them. Hints Imagine trying to run down a street with twenty big crosses lining it. It's so scary that you keep running faster and faster as you go.
readingMnemonic: You figure since you're already on the run that you might as well hone ( ほん ) your running skills while you make your way down this scary, cross lined street. Hints Imagine distracting yourself from the scary crosses by honing your running skills while you do it.

meaningMnemonic: You hoist your towel above your table , drop into the water and sail away. You turned the towel into an actual sail and you're balancing on top of the table, which is now a boat. Hints Imagine sailing out into the open sea, drops of water hitting your face, as the towel sail catches the air and carries you away.
readingMnemonic: As you sail off into the ocean you hear a familiar voice shout out, "Ahoy!" Han ( はん ) Solo calls. He's also got a towel sail, but it's on the Millennium Falcon, which is half-submerged in the water. Hints You sail nervously past Han Solo who also seems to be sailing, though in worse shape than you. But he keeps throwing you finger guns so you figure it's best to just sail on and pretend this never happened.

meaningMnemonic: The flowers that grow on your roof that look like a sleeping bear is sedge . Sedge grow all over the world! Hints You've probably seen them before , you just didn't know what they were called! Looks like a green sleeping bear bum, right?
readingMnemonic: The next time you see a sedge bite into it. It tastes like suga r ( すが )! Luckily, it don't taste like bear. Hints Imagine biting into a sedge flower and tasting the yummy sugary taste. Mmmm.

meaningMnemonic: Pour all of your alcohol in the pool to serve all your guests at once! They can all help themselves to as much or as little alcohol as they want! What a great idea! Hints Imagine serving all of your guests their alcohol by dumping it all in the pool! Now jump in and drink all you want!
readingMnemonic: As you serve your guests (and yourself) you look over and see Shaq ( しゃく ) also trying to serve them. And by serving I mean getting served because he's throwing them into the pool. Hints Picture Shaq serving your guests by tossing them into your alcohol filled pool. Thanks, Shaq... I guess.

meaningMnemonic: Deep in your soul , you feel like you want to pull your fang s out by the root , but instead you let out a loud sigh . You're one of the only people you know that has fangs, and it weighs heavily on your soul. Hints Imagine all of the other people staring and pointing, the kids making fun of you, no one seeing you as equal. And just... sigh. Deep down, you want to get rid of your fangs, but you can't do it.
readingMnemonic: You sigh again and say, "I wish I was just a normal guy ( がい )." I swear the rest of me is a guy like the rest of you. *sigh* Hints Now you're staring in the mirror at yourself. You sigh loudly and take out the pliers. You'll be a guy like everyone else. S-soon. As soon as you can muster up enough strength to stop sighing and rip these fangs out.

meaningMnemonic: This tree turkey has been sitting directly on your spine for weeks straight. The pain is starting to become unbearable, and it seems like no one wants to help you. Hints Tree turkeys are absolutely huge, and this exceptionally large one has been sitting right on top of your spine for what feels like ages. Imagine the pain of a huge turkey pressing down on your spine for weeks, perhaps months. How are you still holding on?!
readingMnemonic: Just as your spine seems to be getting used to the pressure, the tree turkey unleashes a cry: " TWEE T ( つい )!" To your horror, a flock of tree turkeys emerge from the trees. Hints You desperately try to escape from the weight of the tree turkey still sitting on top of your spine, but to no avail. The only thing you can see is dozens of tree turkeys approaching to plant themselves firmly on top of your spine, screaming "TWEET, TWEET".

meaningMnemonic: You see seven sword s just sitting in a hole and so you decide to steal them. They were just left in that hole after all, it's not like anyone was using them. And even if they were, they'll never know you were the one to steal them, right? Hints Imagine seeing seven swords just lying abandoned in a hole. Feel the urge to steal them all. Do it, do it!
readingMnemonic: You steal the swords and realize they aren't just seven random swords, they're from the famous sword sets ( せつ ) they sell online. This particular set is from the Seven Samurai movie. Yes! What a great steal! Hints Imagine your delight as you look up the different sword sets online and realize you happened to steal the best one!

meaningMnemonic: There are stone s that smell like trash in the river . You reach in and realize these rocks are made of sulfur . Even the flow of this water can't hide the stink of these sulfur rocks. Hints If you haven't smelled sulfur before, it smells a bit like rotten eggs. Something that definitely belongs in the trash.
readingMnemonic: You throw the sulfur rock as hard as you can, but it hits someone in the back of the head. Oh no, it's Ryu ( りゅう ) from Street Fighter. You try to apologize and explain that you just didn't want this stinky trash rock, I mean, sulfur rock near you. You didn't know he was there. Hints Ryu looks down at you, holding the sulfurous rock in one hand. Then he uppercuts you with it! Shoryuken!

sentences.english: I realized how difficult managing poultry raising is.

sentences.english: I try to make sure I eat as much white meat from chicken as I can.

meaningMnemonic: Sedge field is both Sugahara and Sugawara , the Japanese family names. Sedgefield is a family name (and a place-name) in English too, so that might help you with this one! Historically, the name has been associated with scholars and writers, including prominent Heian period statesman, scholar, and poet Sugawara-no-michizane ( 菅原道真 ) and noblewoman, writer, and poet Sugawara-no-takasue-no-musume ( 菅原孝標女 ), also known more simply as Lady Sarashina in the English speaking world.

meaningMnemonic: You learned 飽 as "bored," but remember how it could also mean " sated "? Well, the 飽く in this expression means "to be sated." Add on までも , and you get "even until sated." Oh, and this expression has another common use too: purely or strictly . As in, "this is purely hypothetical," or "this is strictly my own opinion."
